comment: What must not silently disappear from netwatch. `prose` names guardrails no code enforces; `split` declares which half of the skill is deterministic; `baseline` names the offline, $0 checks pinned against a real run.

prose.pattern: Every connection in the report is one the skill actually obs
prose.rationale: The one rule. It is the reason this skill exists rather than a prompt; lose the line and the skill becomes a generic assistant with extra steps.

prose.pattern: Never claim a result you did not observe
prose.rationale: Honesty about what was verified is the whole house contract. A skill that reports success it did not witness is worse than one that reports nothing.

The safety boundary that makes this skill runnable without sudo and without capturing anyone's data. Lose the line and a future author reaches for tcpdump, and the skill starts capturing credentials off a shared network — the exact thing the connection-snapshot design exists to avoid.

prose.pattern: An empty capture is never reported as .all clear
prose.rationale: A snapshot taken while nothing was talking, or a capture command that silently failed, must read as 'I saw nothing', not as a clean bill of health. The code refuses zero flows, but the prose is what stops a run from narrating the refusal away.

deterministic.step: parse the captured snapshot into normalized flows, each grounded in its source line
classify each flow known-vs-unrecognized strictly against the baseline and roll up volumes by process and destination
validate and store the baseline of known flows, and report snapshot coverage
fold chosen unrecognized flows into the baseline, reversibly

nondeterministic.step: decide which unrecognized flows are worth investigating and which are ordinary background chatter
nondeterministic.why: an unrecognized connection to an Apple or CDN address looks identical to one to a stranger; only a person knows what this machine's normal is

nondeterministic.step: name what an unknown remote host probably is
nondeterministic.why: reverse DNS gives a hostname, not an owner; whether 17.253.x.x is 'Apple push' or a CDN edge is a reading of context nothing in the snapshot records

nondeterministic.step: decide whether a new destination or a volume spike is worth alarm
nondeterministic.why: a process suddenly moving ten times its usual bytes is either a backup running or something wrong, and the byte count alone does not say which

nondeterministic.step: word each accepted baseline entry so a reader six months later can tell why the flow was allowed
nondeterministic.why: a raw host:port pair is precise and unreadable, and a baseline nobody can interpret is one nobody will dare to prune

_baseline_comment: Pinned against a real run of this skill, never a synthetic fixture. Offline and $0 by construction: no network, no model, so CI cannot spend and cannot flake.

baseline.rationale: the parser dropping a connection while the report still looks complete; a flow losing the source line that grounds it; the classifier calling a flow known when no baseline entry covers it — pinned against a real snapshot captured on the maintainer's own Mac, with flows + report re-run over the frozen capture and the report byte-compared.

the grounding gate weakening until a run reports over zero flows and calls it clean, and the one rule ceasing to be code so the model's hunch can reach the report — pinned against an empty capture, and a report asked to attach a 'dangerous' verdict to an unrecognized flow — both of which must exit non-zero.
